# MCP tool reference

The 6 tools the server offers, read from a running server.

The server is the same code as the CLI, over stdio. Start it with `agent-whatsapp mcp`, or register it with a
client with `agent-whatsapp mcp install --client claude-code --account <organisation>/whatsapp` — a change the
person approves.

**It reads, and never sends.** Every tool reads a local index of the messages WhatsApp for Mac keeps on this
Mac; none sends, marks read, reacts or reaches the network. `whatsapp_draft` returns a link that opens WhatsApp
with the text filled in, and the person presses send. **Every call that acts on an account takes `account`**,
unless the server is pinned to one (`--account`); there is no default. Adding an account and the allow and deny
lists are commands a person runs: no tool changes what an agent may see.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`whatsapp_status`](#whatsapp_status) | What is set up, whether each WhatsApp store can be read (and, when macOS blocks it, exactly what the person must allow), and what the local index holds. |
| [`whatsapp_sync`](#whatsapp_sync) | Copies WhatsApp for Mac’s message store privately (never writing to it), checks the copy, rebuilds the local index from it, and deletes the copy. |
| [`whatsapp_chats`](#whatsapp_chats) | Chats, most recent first, as of the last sync. |
| [`whatsapp_read`](#whatsapp_read) | One chat, newest first, by the id whatsapp_chats shows or a phone number. |
| [`whatsapp_search`](#whatsapp_search) | Words in message text, captions, file names, sender names and chat names, as of the last sync. |
| [`whatsapp_draft`](#whatsapp_draft) | Composes a message and returns a link that opens WhatsApp with the text filled in. |

### `whatsapp_status`

What is set up, whether each WhatsApp store can be read (and, when macOS blocks it, exactly what the person must allow), and what the local index holds. `check: false` skips opening the store.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | string | no | which WhatsApp account, as `organisation/whatsapp` |
| `check` | boolean | no |  |

### `whatsapp_sync`

Copies WhatsApp for Mac’s message store privately (never writing to it), checks the copy, rebuilds the local index from it, and deletes the copy. Every other tool reads that index. May fail with the macOS permission the person has to grant — relay the hint.

*writes · idempotent*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | string | **yes** | which WhatsApp account, as `organisation/whatsapp` |

### `whatsapp_chats`

Chats, most recent first, as of the last sync. Status updates are left out unless `kind` is `status`. Each name arrives inside an untrusted-content envelope. `phone` is set for one-to-one chats; groups and people who hide their number have none.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | string | **yes** | which WhatsApp account, as `organisation/whatsapp` |
| `limit` | integer | no | 1 to 500; 50 when left out |
| `kind` | `direct` \\| `hidden-number` \\| `group` \\| `status` \\| `broadcast` \\| `channel` \\| `unknown` | no |  |

### `whatsapp_read`

One chat, newest first, by the id whatsapp_chats shows or a phone number. Text, captions, sender names and file names are inside untrusted-content envelopes. Media is listed by type, size and name only — never downloaded.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | string | **yes** | which WhatsApp account, as `organisation/whatsapp` |
| `chat` | string | **yes** | a chat id from whatsapp_chats, or a phone number |
| `limit` | integer | no | 1 to 200; 50 when left out |
| `before` | string | no | the `next` value of an earlier read, for older messages |

### `whatsapp_search`

Words in message text, captions, file names, sender names and chat names, as of the last sync. Each word is matched as a word; there is no query syntax. Status updates are searched only when `kind` is `status` or `chat` names one. Results are inside untrusted-content envelopes.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | string | **yes** | which WhatsApp account, as `organisation/whatsapp` |
| `query` | string | **yes** | the words to find |
| `chat` | string | no | only in this chat |
| `sender` | string | no | only from senders whose name contains this |
| `kind` | `direct` \\| `hidden-number` \\| `group` \\| `status` \\| `broadcast` \\| `channel` \\| `unknown` | no | only in one kind of chat |
| `limit` | integer | no | 1 to 100; 20 when left out |

### `whatsapp_draft`

Composes a message and returns a link that opens WhatsApp with the text filled in. It sends nothing and opens nothing: give the person the link; they check the message and press send themselves. `to` is a phone number or any chat id whatsapp_chats or whatsapp_read shows. A group, a chat with a hidden number, a broadcast list or a channel gets the text to paste instead; a status update cannot be drafted to.

*read-only*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | string | no | the account the chat belongs to, as `organisation/whatsapp` |
| `to` | string | **yes** | a phone number with its country code, or a chat id from whatsapp_chats |
| `text` | string | **yes** | the message |
